## Cards generated
- FEAT1 — GitHub issue client for user requests (server lib) (workstream: server)
- FEAT2 — Feedback payload validation + issue body builder (workstream: server)
- FEAT3 — Right-click feedback dialog, mounted globally (workstream: ui)

- FEAT5 — Runbook + CLAUDE.md rows for the feedback loop (workstream: docs)

---

## Brief (owner, verbatim intent)

Add a feature to the merchant console that lets a user file bugs and
request features from the site itself. Right-click anywhere presents a
text box with Okay / Cancel. The user types a phrase; Okay creates a
GitHub issue tagged `UserRequest`. Separately, a dedicated agent runs
`/dev-loop:pull-start` in its own session and pulls those issues from the
kanban plane, implementing them in near real time.

## Why the issue must be kanban-shaped

The pull agent's ready list (`claim-card.sh ready`, Issues backend) only
sees an **open** issue carrying BOTH a `state:backlog` label and an
`id:<ID>` label. A bare `UserRequest` issue is invisible to it. So the
route creates the issue, learns its number, then patches on the id label
and the canonical `<ID> — <title>` title. The id prefix is `REQ`
(registered in `.claude/dev-loop.json` `cardPrefixes`).

## Contract (every card builds to this; nothing here is negotiable)

### Environment (server only)

| Var | Meaning | When absent |
|---|---|---|
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | token with `issues:write` on the target repo | route answers `503 { message: "Feedback is not configured on this server." }` |
| `FEEDBACK_REPO` | `owner/repo` to file into | defaults to `BeauBender/claude-code-training` |

Local dev: `GITHUB_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)" npm run dev` inside
`build-battle/merchant-console`. `.env*` is gitignored; never commit a
token. Tokens never reach the client.

### HTTP: `POST /api/feedback`

Request body (JSON): `{ "text": string, "page": string }`

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | `{ "number": 12, "id": "REQ12", "url": "https://github.com/.../issues/12" }` | filed |
| 400 | `{ "message": <user-safe> }` | validation failed |
| 503 | `{ "message": "Feedback is not configured on this server." }` | no `GITHUB_TOKEN` |
| 502 | `{ "message": "GitHub rejected the request." }` | GitHub non-2xx (log the detail server-side; never echo GitHub's body) |

Same error shape as every other route: a status that means what it says
and a message safe to show.

### Validation (`src/lib/feedback.ts`)

```ts
export type Feedback = { text: string; page: string }
export type ParseResult =
  | { ok: true; value: Feedback }
  | { ok: false; message: string }
export function parseFeedback(input: unknown): ParseResult
export function feedbackTitle(text: string): string
export function feedbackIssueBody(f: Feedback, filedAt: string): string
```

- `text`: must be a string; trimmed; 3 ≤ length ≤ 2000. Otherwise `ok:false`
  with a message that names the rule ("Tell us a little more" / "Keep it
  under 2000 characters").
- `page`: must be a string starting with `/`, ≤ 200 chars, no whitespace.
  Anything else → `ok:false`. This is the allowlist: the page path is
  client input and lands in an issue body, so it is checked, not trusted.
- `feedbackTitle`: first line of the trimmed text, internal whitespace
  collapsed, truncated to 72 chars with a trailing `…` when cut.
- `feedbackIssueBody`: the epic-card shape the pull agent expects, so a
  REQ issue reads like any other card:

```markdown
# <title>

**Type:** user-request

## Goal
<text verbatim, as a Markdown blockquote>

## Context
- Filed from: `<page>`
- Filed at: <filedAt ISO-8601>
- Source: merchant console right-click feedback dialog

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] the request above is addressed in the merchant console
- [ ] gate green: `cd build-battle/merchant-console && npm test && npm run lint`
```

### GitHub client (`src/lib/github.ts`)

```ts
export type IssueClientConfig = {
  token: string
  repo: string            // "owner/repo"
  fetchImpl?: typeof fetch
  apiBase?: string        // default "https://api.github.com"
}
export type CreatedIssue = { number: number; id: string; url: string }
export class GitHubError extends Error { status: number }
export function readGitHubConfig(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): IssueClientConfig | null
export async function createUserRequestIssue(
  cfg: IssueClientConfig, issue: { title: string; body: string },
): Promise<CreatedIssue>
```

- `readGitHubConfig` returns `null` when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is unset/empty;
  `FEEDBACK_REPO` defaults to `BeauBender/claude-code-training`.
- `createUserRequestIssue` does exactly two calls:
  1. `POST {apiBase}/repos/{repo}/issues` with
     `{ title, body, labels: ["UserRequest", "state:backlog"] }`
  2. `PATCH {apiBase}/repos/{repo}/issues/{number}` with
     `{ title: "REQ<number> — <title>", labels: ["UserRequest", "state:backlog", "id:REQ<number>"] }`
- Headers on both: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`,
  `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`, `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28`,
  `Content-Type: application/json`.
- Any non-2xx throws `GitHubError` carrying the status. The function
  never logs or returns the token.
- Labels `UserRequest`, `state:backlog` already exist on the repo (created
  during planning); GitHub also auto-creates missing labels on create.

### UI (`src/components/ui/feedback/`)

- `FeedbackTrigger.tsx` (`"use client"`): on mount, listens for
  `contextmenu` on `document`. When `shouldInterceptContextMenu(event)`
  is true it calls `preventDefault()`, records
  `window.location.pathname` as `page`, and opens the dialog. Removes the
  listener on unmount.
- `shouldInterceptContextMenu` lives in `src/lib/contextmenu.ts` (pure,
  unit-testable, no DOM types beyond a small structural input):
  returns **false** when `shiftKey` is held (Shift + right-click is the
  escape hatch to the browser's native menu), when `defaultPrevented` is
  already true, or when the target is editable (`input`, `textarea`,
  `select`, or `contentEditable`). True otherwise.
- `FeedbackDialog.tsx`: Radix Dialog (`@radix-ui/react-dialog`, the same
  primitive `Drawer.tsx` uses). Accessible name "Send feedback". One
  labelled `<textarea>` ("Describe the bug or the feature you need").
  Buttons from `@/components/Button`: **Cancel** (secondary) and **Okay**
  (primary; disabled while the trimmed text is empty or while submitting).
  Okay → `fetch("/api/feedback", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ text, page }) })`.
  States: idle → submitting → success (shows `REQ<n>` as a link to `url`,
  a Close button) | error (shows the server `message`, keeps the text,
  Okay retries). Escape / Cancel close and clear. Focus moves into the
  textarea on open and returns on close (Radix does this; do not fight it).
  Tailwind only; no inline `style`.
- Mount: `src/app/layout.tsx` renders `<FeedbackTrigger />` once inside
  `ThemeProvider`, next to `SidebarProvider`. Nothing else in layout
  changes.

### Tests

`vitest` here is Node-only (no jsdom) and only picks up `src/**/*.test.ts`.
So: pure logic is unit-tested (`feedback.test.ts`, `github.test.ts` with an
injected `fetchImpl`, `contextmenu.test.ts`); React components are not —
their correctness is carried by the tested predicates they call and by
`npm run lint`. Do not add jsdom or a component-testing dependency.

### Gate

`cd build-battle/merchant-console && npm test && npm run lint` green on
every card.

## The agent side (operational, not code)

In a second terminal, open Claude Code at the repo root and run
`/dev-loop:pull-start`. Every REQ issue is a ready card (`claim-card.sh
ready`) the moment it is filed, because it carries `state:backlog` +
`id:REQ<n>`; the Stop hook nudges the session to keep pulling until
`/dev-loop:pull-stop`. FEAT5 writes this down as `docs/feedback-loop.md`.

## Out of scope

Screenshots/attachments, auth or rate limiting on the route (internal
tool, local dev), editing or listing issues from the console, a Cards
page, any persistence layer (NWP-203).
